newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds slip in step with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds slip in step with Treasuries.

text.p: Light selling and profit-taking sent prices of U.S. mortgage-backed securities lower on Monday, mostly in line with Treasuries, analysts and traders said.
But mortgages pared earlier losses, trading off 1/32 to 4/32 overall by late afternoon. Spreads were mostly flat, since comparable Treasuries were off 4/32 to 5/32.
"We popped here because of a little short-covering, really that's about it," one trader said.
Another trader said some interest-rate hike jitters permeated the market following a strong housing report.

At 1300 EST/1800 GMT, the National Association of Home Builders said its market index hit 58 in March, up from 54 in February, a sign of continued strength in the housing sector. That increased market players' fears that the Federal Reserve Bank will rein in credit at the March 25 policy meeting, analysts said.

A Fed tightening would increase market volatility and disrupt mortgage spreads on an option-adjusted spread (OAS) basis, causing them to widen, said Cynthia Rivera, mortgage analyst at BZW Securities.
"Immediately, it's not going to be very good for mortgages," said Rivera. "But once the dust settles, and the market stabilizes a little ... (mortgages) will be better off."
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 3/32 at 99-03/32, yielding 95 basis points over the 10-yeaer Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 3/32 lower as well, at 99-05/32 and 99-11/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 5/32 at 96-21/32 bid, yielding 6.72 percent.
